A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SNAP-UQ. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including Appendices A–O in v1 and A–Q in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original MCU resource measurements, monitoring and failure-detection results, calibration scores, and ablations in Tables 1–15.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds calibration, robust-head, deployment, training-cost, and seed-robustness results, including Tables 5, 16–17, and 30–31.

M1.justification: The core predictor architecture, auxiliary objective, uncertainty score, and robust likelihood variants remain. Appendix Q.2 adds an explicit post-hoc training option: train the classifier first, freeze its backbone, then train the prediction heads. This extends v1's joint training and optional activation detachment.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, SpeechCommands, their corruption streams, and the same semantic OOD sources. Additional TinyImageNet scores and model/deployment stress tests expand results and settings without adding a new data population or prediction task.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds MCD, HYDRA, and QUTE to the reported failure-detection comparison. New ID comparisons include QUTE+ in Table 6, and Table 31 evaluates Tiny-DEEP. The ReAct, ASH, energy, and Mahalanobis comparisons already present in v1's Appendix O are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce ID-only versus ID+CID calibration controls, robust-head parameter sweeps, four/five-tap configurations, and ID F1 reporting. Table 17 additionally identifies a ResNet-50 TinyImageNet setting. Appendix N.11 specifies a separate 600 MHz Cortex-M7 profiling protocol with warm-up and 100 kS/s power sampling; the main evaluation setup is largely retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds raw-versus-calibrated scoring, quantitative Student-t/Huber comparisons, tap-correlation analyses, controlled BN/int8 rescaling checks, runtime decomposition, and training-overhead analyses. The two-tap leave-one-out study in v1 Table 9 is replaced by a four-tap study in v2 Table 13.

E5.justification: v1 specifies three seeds and 1,000-resample bootstrap intervals. v2 Appendix Q.5 explicitly reports expansion from three to ten seeds for the checks in Table 31, with means, standard errors, and numerical confidence intervals. Table 6 adds ID mean±standard-deviation reporting, while Table 30 averages five training runs. Three-seed reporting remains elsewhere.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive ID, calibration, robust-head, tap, profiling, and training-cost results. Most headline SNAP-UQ scores and Appendix O results remain unchanged. Existing Table 3 values also change: EE-ensemble's MNIST OOD AUROC falls from 0.87 to 0.85, and DEEP's SpeechCommands OOD AUROC from 0.92 to 0.91.

T1.justification: The principal propositions and Woodbury derivations remain. Appendix L corrects projector complexity by including the input-channel factor, changing HWr to HWCinr. Appendix G removes explicit Gaussian/robust-loss gradient derivations and the adaptive-weight update formula. Appendix P primarily adds empirical verification rather than new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: single-pass, compact depth-wise uncertainty estimation that improves corrupted-stream monitoring and calibration under MCU constraints. The headline resource-saving claims remain; added evidence and stronger novelty wording do not redefine their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of tap complementarity, robust-head selection, runtime savings, threshold portability, and quantization invariance in Appendices N–P. The shortened conclusion omits v1's explicit caveat about untested modalities and longer field deployments, while retaining limitations concerning activation access, covariance approximation, and tap selection.

D1.justification: v2 adds robust-head tuning grids and defaults, Student-t logarithm-LUT implementation and memory details, profiling clock/warm-up/power-sampling information, and measured training time and memory overhead. Table 1 also newly explains BASE's entropy/statistics overhead and SNAP-UQ's kernel fusion. Most original training schedules and export details are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Tiny Deep Ensemble, alongside new citations concerning MCU runtimes, quantization, calibration, and OOD detection. Earlier Brier/proper-scoring-rule and Jacob quantization references are removed. The central positioning against confidence-only and multipass uncertainty methods remains.

P1.justification: Section 2 and much of Appendices A–H are extensively rewritten, often replacing compact lists and displayed formulas with explanatory paragraphs. Algorithms move to the appendices, the conclusion is condensed, and new appendix sections, terminology clarification, and an LLM-use statement alter the document's organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous result tables, a notation table, and new correlation, tap-count, and runtime figures. Existing tables gain context rows or notes and are resized or relocated. Algorithms 1–2 move out of the main text; v1 Figures 8–9 are retained as v2 Figures 11–12 rather than newly added analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful controls, training-cost evidence, and explicit ten-seed estimates that v1 lacked. However, important new evidence is inconsistent: Figure 8 reports self-correlations of 0.60–0.78 rather than 1, and Table 17's TinyImageNet Brier scores of 0.058–0.060 exceed the maximum 0.01 permitted by Appendix F.4's class-normalized definition for 200 classes. These unresolved problems undermine the expanded validation, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
